title: Egress proxy + NACL orchestration and private DNS Terraform module
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a composable Terraform module that enforces outbound egress controls for Private deployments: orchestrate security group defaults, network ACLs (stateless edge rules), an optional egress-proxy/NAT pattern, and automated private DNS (Route53 private hosted zone) attachments. The module must be safe to apply against existing customer VPCs (non-destructive by default), provide clear upgrade/migration steps, expose diagnostic outputs for health checks, and include Terratest/CI checks. This work is intended to consolidate ad-hoc customer scripts into a single supported Terraform module that Redwood customers can enable in Private and Dedicated deployments.
goals: Provide opinionated defaults for egress (deny-by-default with allow-lists) implementable with security groups and NACLs
Add optional managed egress-proxy (autoscaled EC2/ALB or serverless forwarder) and a NAT fallback mode
Automate private DNS zone association and resolver endpoints for on-prem/VPC hybrid setups
Include non-destructive upgrade path and migration helpers for customers with existing firewall rules
Ship health-check outputs and a small diagnostics lambda that reports config drift and connectivity to Redwood control plane
acceptance_criteria: Module can be applied to an existing VPC without dropping established connections by default
Security group + NACL combination enforces outbound policy and passes synthetic traffic tests in CI
Optional egress-proxy deploys and routes traffic for test workload; NAT fallback available
Private hosted zone auto-association works across up to 5 subnets; documented limits included
Module exposes outputs used by Console: egress_policy_status, private_dns_associations, proxy_endpoint
Automated Terratest suite runs in pipeline and validates failing/allow rules and DNS resolution
implementation_notes: Module will be split into submodules: sg-defaults, nacl-edge, egress-proxy, private-dns-assoc, diagnostics
Use provider constraints to support AWS >= 4.60 and pin to supported modules; avoid hard provider aliasing where possible
Design var schema to allow three modes: permissive (no change), enforce (apply deny-by-default), and audit-only (cloudwatch/diag events)
Diagnostics implemented as a lightweight Lambda that runs periodic checks and writes to CloudWatch Metric + EventBridge
When egress-proxy enabled, module should register ALB target group and update route table via provided integration hooks
Plan/apply should surface a clear migration plan: show proposed rule additions and destructive changes explicitly and require a confirm flag to perform rule replacements
testing_strategy: Unit: terraform validate + tflint in PRs
Integration: Terratest scenarios (fresh VPC, existing VPC with preexisting SGs/NACLs, DNS-only mode)
End-to-end: deploy sample customer stack in sandbox account, exercise traffic through proxy and NAT to public endpoints
Chaos: simulate broken route table and verify diagnostics alerts and Console rollback guidance
migration_plan: Phase 1: audit-only mode - run module in audit-only to collect drift and recommend rule deltas
Phase 2: staged enforce - enable in non-prod VPCs, run CI tests and manual verification
Phase 3: customer opt-in for prod: provide a migration script that creates replacement SGs/NACLs and keeps old rules for 7 days
Rollback: module supports a revert toggle that re-applies previous rule set from saved state bucket
security_considerations: All secrets and proxy certs must reference customer-managed KMS keys or HSM where available
Least-privilege IAM roles for module-managed resources; avoid broad wildcard policies
Diagnostics lambda must redact customer identifiers before sending telemetry to Redwood; send only aggregated metrics
Module should document potential impact on cross-account VPC peering and recommend explicit allow-lists
deliverables: Confluence runbook with migration steps and rollback playbook
GitHub PR template that runs validate+tflint+terratest
Console integration spec for new outputs (egress_policy_status, proxy_endpoint)
